WATCH: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. says the problem with the design of the Sunog Apog Station is already solved during an onsite inspection on Monday (May 25, 2026) in Tondo, Manila.

He said Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso has been complaining about the annual flooding experienced by the residents in the area, especially during habagat season or typhoons due to the faulty pumping station.

Apart from the improvement of the electrical equipment, Marcos also directed the Department of Public Works and Highways to conduct regular cleaning of pumping stations to prevent them from being clogged with garbage. | Teresa Montemayor (Video courtesy of MPC Pool)

LOOK: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. inspects the Delpan Sports Complex and the Delpan Evacuation Center in Manila, which are serving as temporary shelters for more than 2,000 families displaced by a fire in Parola Compound over the weekend.

The fire victims received P10,000 in cash assistance, as well as food and hygiene kits from the Department of Social Welfare and Development.

In a brief statement, Marcos said assistance would be provided until the victims get back on their feet. | 📸: MPC pool via @luisacabatoINQ

LOOK: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., with DPWH Sec. Vince Dizon, inspects the Sunog Apog Pumping Station, an infrastructure project aimed at mitigating chronic flooding in low-lying areas, in Tondo, Manila, on Monday.

Marcos ordered the reactivation of the P774-million Sunog Apog Pumping station this June to help ease the severe flooding that residents experience and complain about every year, adding that he received complaints from residents that the pumping station had been non-operational for six years, causing difficulties whenever floodwaters rise, especially during the southwest monsoon or typhoons. | 📷: Marianne Bermudez, Philippine Daily Inquirer
